paragraphs: FeedbackFruits sells teaching activities that run inside a university's own learning management system, so neither instructors nor students need a second login. The activities pull assessment, collaboration and feedback into a course in a few clicks.

Peer Review carries the whole process from assignment submission through to graded feedback. An instructor decides whether students review each other individually or as teams. They also decide whether feedback is anonymous or attributed. An AI companion called Acai offers coaching, grading and content creation to cut the work faculty carry. It can generate discussion prompts and quiz questions to speed up course design. A newer activity, Oral Practice, has students talk through their reasoning with that AI or with a peer, around work they submitted or a skill. Every session is recorded and stored without extra admin.

The site claims use at more than 200 institutions worldwide. It also counts over 5,000 educators. Testimonials on the peer review page are attributed to staff such as a director of academic technology at a school of public health. An institution can start with a supported pilot before committing further. The company points to recognised security standards and certifications, and offers human support to teachers and students five days a week.

quote.text: When AI makes it easy to produce convincing work without genuine understanding, submitted outputs stop being reliable evidence of learning.
